title: Word Search
statement: Return True if the word can be traced in the grid by moving to horizontally or vertically adjacent cells, never using the same cell twice in one path.

hints.1_question: Start a search from every cell that matches the first letter. What do you need to remember during one path so you don't reuse a cell?
hints.2_nudge: DFS from each start: match the next letter in the 4 directions, mark the current cell as used, and UNMARK it when you return so other paths can use it.
hints.3_big_hint: dfs(r, c, i): if i == len(word) True; if out of bounds or mismatch False; mark cell; try 4 neighbours; restore the cell; return result.

known_bugs.name: does not restore the cell after exploring (no backtracking)
known_bugs.followup: After a path fails, is the cell you marked usable by a different path? What does your code do to it?

known_bugs.name: allows reusing a cell within one path
known_bugs.followup: Can the same cell be used twice in one word? How do you prevent it?

known_bugs.name: only moves right or down
known_bugs.followup: Which directions may a path move in according to the statement?

followups: How can you prune the search (check letter frequencies, search the rarer end first)?
